hook.text: A sword tap on the shoulder makes a commoner a knight. One gesture changes your legal status.

buildup.text: Medieval knighthood required years of service as a page, then squire. The ceremony was the final exam.

discovery.text: The accolade—the actual dubbing—was often preceded by a full night of prayer and fasting.

twist.text: British knighthoods are now honorary. Sir Elton John and Sir Patrick Stewart share the same title as medieval warriors.

climax.text: Knighthood endures because people need visible markers of earned status. The sword is just a prop.

punchline.text: The sword changes nothing. The title changes everything.

quiz.question: What is the 'accolade' in the context of knighthood?
options: The act of dubbing with a sword
